record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Formulate the positive-tree principles obtained by replacing measure with dimension in the definitions of P^+, P, and P^−. How do the implication and non-implication results for these principles change in that dimension-based setting?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. How about using dimension? (Define the above concepts by replacing measure by dimension.)

artifact.status_search_result: The dimension-based variants are explicitly posed as an open problem in a 2025 collection of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory; no resolution or partial result for the dimension analogues was found.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 11 asks how the positive-tree principles P+, P, P- behave when measure is replaced with dimension; no answer is given.
status_evidence.claim: The dimension analogue of the positive-tree principles is posed as an open problem.
